paragraphs.text: Quick prompt templates for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): global and per-session templates, floating panel
+ right-sidebar tab, scheduled auto-injection (silent or chat-visible), SQLite persistence, sync CLI
# @nelsonlongxiang/dsh-prompt-templates
English | 中文
Quick prompt templates for DeepSeek Harness: global and per-session templates, a right-side browser
panel, and pure-TS SQLite persistence via `node:sqlite` — one self-contained plugin, installable wit
-TS SQLite persistence via `node:sqlite` — one self-contained plugin, installable with `dsh plugin`.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart `dsh web`, then look for the templates button in the composer tool row. Since 0.12.0 the sam
e library is also a **right-sidebar tab**: open it from the sidebar's `+` guide page (entry “Prompt
templates”) — it lives beside the conversation, keeps the composer visible, and always targets the s
ession the sidebar is viewing. On hosts without the sidebar services the tab stays dormant and the f
loating panel keeps working.
No Python toolchain required — since 0.3.0 the host half persists templates through `node:sqlite` (N
ode ≥ 24) directly inside the host process, reading and writing the same `$DSH_HOME/ext/prompt-templ
ates/db.sqlite3` the former Python child owned (zero data migration).
## What you get
- **Global + per-session templates** — globals apply everywhere; session templates stay private to o

ne conversation and can be promoted to global in one click
- **Scheduled auto-injection** — per-temp
late switch and interval: the host re-surfaces an enabled template into the model context at the fir
st request of every Nth round, persisted in SQLite and logged as a durable session event; click the
toolbar `⟳N` badge to open the session's last 20 injections (turn, time, template names, injected bo

dies)
- **Template variables** — content supports `{{date}}` `{{time}}` `{{datetime}}` `{{weekday}}`
`{{session}}` `{{turn}}`, expanded at delivery across insert, send-now, interject, and scheduled in

jection; unresolved values stay literal and storage keeps the raw text
- **Cross-instance sharing**
— copy one template or a whole category as a clipboard payload; paste-import on the target instance

with an explicit same-name overwrite confirm
- **Insert or send** — one click inserts the template a
t the composer caret (or replaces the current selection); send-now dispatches immediately; edit, del

ete, and make-global all live in the row
- **Right-sidebar tab** — the full library also docks as a
sidebar tab (DSH ≥ 0.2.x): open it from the `+` guide and it follows the session you are viewing; th

e floating panel remains for quick one-shot use
- **Search & scroll** — filter the list as you type,

reliable scrolling for long collections
- **Drag to reposition, double-click to reset** — the panel

remembers where you put it
- **Durable by design** — templates persist in SQLite through a pure-TS
store (`node:sqlite`) owned by the host plugin and closed with its lifecycle
## Sharing (cross-instance copy)
- The row ⧉ button shares **one template**; the category tab ⧉ shares **a whole category** (member t

emplates + the category definition)
- The payload is self-describing JSON (`format`/`version` marker

s) carried over the clipboard — no files, no network
- Paste into the toolbar **Import** box on the
target instance: missing categories are created, and **same-name same-scope templates raise an expli
cit overwrite confirm** — overwrite updates the existing row (content/description/category/inject fa

cts), declining skips; the result reports created/overwritten/skipped counts
- What is shared is the
**raw text**: `{{date}}`/`{{turn}}` re-expand at delivery on the receiving instance
## Auto-inject
Each template (global or session-scoped) carries its own **switch + interval N**. When on, the host
injects the template at the first request of every Nth round of the conversation — N=5 means rounds
5, 10, 15, …; rounds count user→assistant exchanges and keep their numbering across restarts.
- The injected content arrives as one durable `<system-reminder>` user message recorded in the sessi
on log (source kind `prompt-template-schedule`), so replays and audits reconstruct exactly what the

model saw
- A boundary round is never injected twice, even across restarts or step retries
- Config
persists in the plugin's SQLite database (schema v4); the deployment can silence everything with `in

jectEnabled: false` in the patch config
- Each template picks a delivery mode: **silent** (default,
model context only) or **visible in chat** (rendered as a normal user message with a ⚙️ scheduled-in
nly) or **visible in chat** (rendered as a normal user message with a ⚙️ scheduled-injection header)
## Template variables
Placeholders `{{date}}` `{{time}}` `{{datetime}}` `{{weekday}}` `{{session}}` `{{turn}}` expand **at
delivery time** — insert, send-now, interject, and scheduled injection all expand:
- Clock variables read the local clock; `{{session}}` is the target session id; `{{turn}}` resolves

only on the scheduled-injection path (it stays literal on insert/send)
- Unknown names pass through

untouched — nothing is silently deleted; the template form shows a variable hint line
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The store is pure TS inside the host half; no child process is spawned.
## Security
- Template content reaches a model request in exactly two ways: as ordinary user text the user chose
to insert, or as scheduled auto-injection of templates where the switch was explicitly enabled — ev

ery injection is a durable session event
- The panel talks to the host store over the Host's plugin
routes only; no extra listener, no outbound network
## Known limitations
- **Session templates need a current session** — with no session open, only global templates are rea

chable
- **Injections don't render in the chat transcript** — the DSH chat view omits injected conte
xt rows by design (they carry a non-`user` message source); see them in the trajectory tab. Template

s with delivery mode **visible** are the exception: they render as ordinary user messages
- **Instal
l from the npm registry, not from a Git URL** — the plugin compiles against the DSH harness checkout
; `pnpm add github:<user>/<repo>` fails at the prepare build step because the published `@deepseek-a
i/*` npm snapshots lag the harness source. Use `dsh plugin --profile <name> add @nelsonlongxiang/dsh
-prompt-templates` instead
